docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Surgical equipment, recurring consumables and vision care
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/supplemental-info/2025-Annual-Report.pdf; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-05-05

Alcon is an eye-care company with Surgical and Vision Care businesses. Surgical includes equipment, procedure-related consumables and implantables such as intraocular lenses. Vision Care includes contact lenses and ocular-health products. These categories have different growth, margin and regulatory characteristics.

Surgical equipment can create recurring demand for consumables and service as clinicians perform procedures. Installed systems, training, workflow familiarity and product compatibility may support retention. The economic claim requires evidence of continued procedure utilization and consumable capture, not merely counting machines once sold.

In Q1 2026, Surgical revenue was $1.460 billion: $438 million implantables, $769 million consumables and $253 million equipment/other. Reported growth was 4%, 8% and 27%, respectively; constant-currency growth was 1%, 4% and 23%. New equipment strength therefore coexists with weak implantable momentum.

Vision Care revenue was $1.225 billion. Contact lenses were $738 million, up 7% reported and 4% currency-neutral, while ocular health was $487 million, up 13% reported and 10% currency-neutral. Dry-eye products including Systane and Tryptyr supported ocular-health growth.

Demand can benefit from aging populations, prevalence of visual impairment, access to care and willingness to adopt premium correction. Those secular factors do not remove competition, reimbursement, physician preferences or affordability constraints. Contact lenses also require manufacturing quality and efficient capacity utilization.

David Endicott is CEO. Management emphasizes innovation, surgical-platform launches, commercial execution and manufacturing efficiency. Unity and Tryptyr are current operating programs; AURN001 is a separate developmental clinical asset, discussed in D09.

FY2025 sales were $10.319 billion, with 13.2% reported operating margin and 19.8% core margin. The large difference reflects material adjustments and must not be ignored. Q1 core margin was 21.2%, while reported margin was 10.9%.

The moat case combines installed workflows, clinical trust, product breadth, distribution and scale in development/manufacturing. It is not equivalent to a patent-guaranteed perpetual annuity. The central question is whether recurring consumables and vision-care earnings remain predictable enough to underwrite the business without requiring success from an unapproved therapy.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three-year operating and cash evidence before the new launch cycle
Source: compiled from: https://investor.alcon.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2025/Alcon-Reports-Full-Year-2024-Results-with-Strong-Top-line-and-Earnings-Growth-and-Record-Cash-Generation/default.aspx; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1167379/000116737926000013/q42025pressrelease.htm; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/supplemental-info/2025-Annual-Report.pdf; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-05-05

Dollar amounts are millions except EPS. Fiscal years end December31. Alcon reports under IFRS; “core” measures are non-IFRS adjustments, not interchangeable with reported earnings. The company-defined FCF measure includes purchases and sales of property/equipment.

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Q1 2026 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net sales | 9,370 | 9,836 | 10,319 | 2,685 |
| Reported operating income | 1,039 | 1,413 | 1,360 | Not separately extracted |
| Reported operating margin | 11.1% | 14.4% | 13.2% | 10.9% |
| Core operating margin | 19.7% | 20.6% | 19.8% | 21.2% |
| Reported diluted EPS | 1.96 | 2.05 | 1.98 | 0.39 |
| Core diluted EPS | 2.74 | 3.05 | 3.07 | 0.85 |
| Operating cash flow | 1,388 | 2,077 | 2,271 | 418 |
| Property/equipment purchases | 658 | 473 | 543 | 139 |
| Company-defined FCF | 730 | 1,604 | 1,733 | 279 |

The FY2025 difference between CFO less purchases and defined FCF reflects property-sale treatment; the table preserves the published FCF rather than forcing exact equality with gross purchases. FY2025 sales grew5% reported and4% constant currency, while core EPS barely increased in reported dollars and core margin declined.

The company returned$848million during2025, including$682million repurchases and$166million dividends. Repurchases retired approximately8.4million shares. This is an observed capital return, separate from the new authorization announced inMay2026.

At March31, cash/equivalents were$1.578billion. Financial debt was$577million current plus$4.157billion noncurrent, total$4.734billion. Calculated net debt was$3.156billion. Q1 diluted weighted-average shares were490.2million and reported net income$189million.

Q1 FCF increased through operating generation, but launches, R&D, tariffs and working capital affect quarterly conversion. A growing equipment base can require upfront spending before consumables mature.

A consistent ROIC series, maintenance/growth capex split and full three-year capital-return table were not extracted. The operating and cash evidence nevertheless establishes a substantial existing business independent of developmental clinical success, while preserving the distinction between core and reported profitability.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: May5 — launch-driven growth with weak implantable momentum
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf; https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/swiss-eye-care-firm-alcons-quarterly-revenue-rises-driven-by-product-launches-2026-05-06
Date: 2026-05-06

Alcon reported Q1 sales$2.685billion, up10% reported and6% constant currency. Surgical grew10% reported/6% currency-neutral to$1.460billion; Vision Care grew9%/6% to$1.225billion. Management highlighted Unity and Tryptyr launch momentum.

Implantables revenue was$438million, up4% reported but only1% constant currency. Consumables were$769million, up8%/4%, and equipment/other$253million, up27%/23%. The largest relative growth came from equipment, while the premium-lens/implantable question remains live.

Contact lenses grew7% reported and4% currency-neutral to$738million. Ocular health grew13%/10% to$487million, supported by dry-eye products. These different categories should not be assumed to carry identical incremental margins.

Reported gross margin was56.8%; core gross margin63.0%. Reported operating margin was10.9% and core21.2%. Higher R&D and launch-related selling/marketing expense, plus incremental tariffs, weighed on margins; operating leverage and manufacturing efficiency provided offsets.

Reported diluted EPS was$0.39 and core$0.85. CFO was$418million and FCF$279million. These figures provide an existing cash-earnings base, but the core-to-reported reconciliation remains economically meaningful.

The company maintained constant-currency sales-growth guidance of5–7%, projected core-margin improvement of70–170basis points, and raised core EPS-growth guidance to10–13% constant currency. The release does not provide an exact USD EPS range in the extracted table.

Net tariff expense after mitigation is estimated at$100–150million for2026. The reduction from February expectations is intended to be reinvested in the business, not automatically retained entirely as extra profit. Capex is expected in the mid-single digits as a share of sales.

The board authorized$1.5billion repurchases over three years. Authorization is not completed execution. A CHF0.28 dividend was approved; no USD yield is invented without the relevant exchange rate.

Reuters reports sales below the$2.71billion LSEG consensus, despite the10% headline increase. That modest sales miss and weak implantables help explain why a growing business can disappoint the market. No second-quarter result or later clinical status belongs in this snapshot.

Guidance is a management forecast, not an observed outcome. The review should model slower adoption and persistent spending as downside scenarios rather than extrapolate the launch quarter mechanically.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: June30 — a core-versus-reported earnings valuation
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ALC/history/?period1=1782777600&period2=1782864000; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1167379/000116737926000013/q42025pressrelease.htm; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-06-30

NYSE-listed Alcon closed June30 at$67.10 on1,973,200 shares. The session opened$67.61 and ranged$66.92–68.22. This historical unadjusted US-dollar close is not the Swiss listing or the present-day quote on the source page.

Using490.2million Q1 diluted weighted-average shares gives a calculated equity-value proxy of$32.892billion. Adding$3.156billion calculated net financial debt gives an EV proxy of$36.048billion. Both use older denominators and are not exact cutoff capitalization.

| Calculated historical measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Price / FY2025 reported EPS$1.98 | 33.9x |
| Price / FY2025 core EPS$3.07 | 21.9x |
| FY2025 defined FCF/equity proxy | 5.3% |
| EV/FY2025 reported operating income$1.360bn | 26.5x |

The substantial core-versus-reported gap matters. A low ratio to core EPS alone does not establish that every excluded cost is economically irrelevant. The EV ratio uses EBIT, not EBITDA, and no harmonized adjusted EV/EBITDA is supplied.

As a sensitivity only, applying10–13% constant-currency growth to$3.07 gives$3.377–3.469 core EPS and a19.3–19.9x ratio. That is not management's USD guidance or verified analyst consensus: currency translation and guidance definitions can change the actual dollar denominator.

The5.3% FCF yield uses company-defined$1.733billion2025 FCF. It does not assign value to unapproved AURN001 sales or assume all current investment costs disappear. Capital expenditure, launch expense and R&D must remain part of the long-term cash model.

An exact cutoff52-week range, own historical forward-P/E distribution, consensus forward EPS and same-date S&P500 forward multiple were not verified. A reliable historical comparison requires matched dates and consistent adjusted earnings rather than an unsupported claim about the normal multiple.

Exact option value for developmental therapy is not calculated. A defensible base valuation should work without approval, with separate upside/downside treatment of clinical risk. The current stock price and observable FCF provide a starting point, not a completed prospective-return analysis.

Required returns should also account for currency exposure, competitive reinvestment and uncertainty over how quickly the spending cycle translates into distributable earnings.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Forecast credibility, margin recovery and clinical risk
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/swiss-eye-care-firm-alcons-quarterly-revenue-rises-driven-by-product-launches-2026-05-06; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/alcon-slides-revenue-misses-forecasts-093207938.html; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-05-06

Reuters' May6 account reports quarterly sales$2.69billion versus$2.71billion consensus, with implantables almost stagnant on an underlying basis. The precise primary figure is1% constant-currency implantable growth. The distinction prevents a modest reported increase from concealing a weak underlying category.

Investing.com's Vahid Karaahmetovic, May6, reports shares down around7% despite a raised full-year earnings outlook. Its framing combines a revenue miss with sharply lower reported operating profit. That is a dated market reaction, not a later investor's retrospective description.

The bear mechanism is that equipment and product launches create growth without delivering the expected durable margin expansion. Selling expense, development cost, manufacturing ramp-up and tariffs may persist longer than assumed. A company can have valuable products and still produce lower returns than its valuation requires.

FY2025 core margin fell from20.6% to19.8%, while reported margin fell from14.4% to13.2%. That history makes the2026 margin-improvement promise something to prove. Q1 core margin21.2% is encouraging, but a single quarter does not establish a steady25%-plus structural margin.

Tariff mitigation is not a free earnings windfall. Management expects$100–150million net expense and plans to reinvest savings relative to the prior outlook. Competitors, currencies, procedure mix and pricing can affect realized profitability independently.

Surgical share and consumable capture are also important. A growing installed base does not guarantee every future procedure uses the expected products at the expected price. Physician preference, reimbursement and competing platforms can change the economics.

AURN001 adds clinical and regulatory uncertainty. Its Phase3 program is underway, but success is not established and no approval or commercial revenue is assumed. If the investment only works with a favorable trial outcome, it becomes a different risk proposition from owning an established recurring-consumables franchise.

Counterevidence includes positive underlying growth in both divisions, improving cash generation, new product uptake and substantial existing FCF. The decision requires separating temporary investment burdens from lasting margin impairment, and separating an optional clinical asset from the core business's forecastability.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Contact lenses and surgical eye-care competitors
Source: compiled from: https://investor.coopercos.com/news-releases/news-release-details/coopercompanies-announces-second-quarter-2026-results; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1860742/000186074226000060/ex991q1-2026.htm; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-06-04

CooperCompanies' CooperVision and Bausch+Lomb provide useful operating comparisons. Their product mix, financial reporting and capital structures differ from Alcon's; neither is a perfect pure-play equivalent to the combined surgical and vision-care business.

Cooper's June4 release reports fiscal Q2 revenue$1.082billion, up8% reported and5% organic. CooperVision revenue was$723.5million, up8% reported and4% constant currency/organic. This is a direct contact-lens demand benchmark close to Alcon's4% currency-neutral lens growth.

Cooper reported corporate gross margin68% and non-GAAP operating margin27%, up260basis points. Those figures include other operations and adjustments. They cannot be used as an exact margin target for Alcon without segment and accounting reconciliation.

Bausch+Lomb's April29 release reports Q1 revenue$1.244billion, up9% reported and6% constant currency. Vision Care was$711million, up8%/5%, and Surgical$228million, up7% reported but1% currency-neutral. Pharmaceuticals contributed another$305million.

| Relevant underlying growth | Alcon Q1 | Bausch+Lomb Q1 | CooperVision fiscal Q2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vision/contact category | Contact lenses4% | Vision Care5% | Contact-lens business4% |
| Surgical |6% total; implantables1% |1% total | Not comparable |

The categories are not identical, but the data show positive vision-care demand across competitors. Weak Alcon implantables cannot be assumed to reflect an industry-wide collapse, nor should stronger equipment growth be assumed permanent.

The competitive moat depends on clinical outcomes, surgeon workflow, distribution, brand, manufacturing quality and innovation. Broad demographic tailwinds benefit multiple companies and do not guarantee Alcon gains share or expands margins.

Peer capital intensity also matters. Contact-lens manufacturing requires capacity and quality investment, while surgical equipment can create downstream consumable economics. A simple gross-margin ranking does not capture those different reinvestment needs.

Cutoff peer forward P/E, EV/EBITDA, ROIC and harmonized FCF yields were not authenticated. No precise relative-value ranking is invented. The operating evidence provides a grounded benchmark for testing management's growth/margin expectations and distinguishing market demand from company-specific execution.

Fiscal-calendar differences also limit direct quarter-to-quarter comparisons.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: New products, clinical development and the May earnings reset
Source: compiled from: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drug-trials-snapshot-tryptyr; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1167379/000116737926000013/q42025pressrelease.htm; https://aurionbiotech.com/2026/04/08/aurion-biotech-doses-first-patients-in-astra-phase-3-study-evaluating-aurn001-in-patients-with-corneal-edema-secondary-to-corneal-endothelial-dysfunction; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ALC/history/?period1=1782777600&period2=1782864000
Date: 2026-06-30

May28,2025: FDA approved Tryptyr for adult dry-eye disease, according to its later2025 trial snapshot. That approval concerns an existing ocular-health product and must not be confused with AURN001, which remains developmental.

During2025: Alcon invested in new products and surgical-platform commercialization. Full-year revenue eventually reached$10.319billion, while core margin declined to19.8%. Stronger cash generation coexisted with disappointing margin progression.

February24,2026: Alcon reported full-year results, including$2.271billion CFO,$1.733billion defined FCF and$3.07 core EPS. Its report documents an existing profitable business independent of any unapproved cell therapy.

April8: Aurion announced first patients dosed in the ASTRA Phase3 trial of AURN001 for corneal edema secondary to endothelial dysfunction. The study is a pivotal clinical program, not approval or established commercial success. D09 separates the option from the core case.

May5: Q1 results showed10% reported sales growth,6% currency-neutral growth and21.2% core margin. Unity and Tryptyr supported growth; implantables grew only1% currency-neutral. Management raised core EPS-growth guidance and authorized$1.5billion repurchases.

May6: Reuters reported the modest sales miss against$2.71billion consensus. Independent market coverage described shares down around7%, despite the improved earnings outlook. That is the principal dated operating/expectations dislocation in this evidence set.

June4: CooperCompanies reported positive contact-lens growth, adding a fresh demand benchmark. Bausch+Lomb had also reported growth in April. Industry demand is not uniformly absent, leaving company execution and mix relevant.

June30: Alcon closed$67.10. This is the current public-information review date, without asserting any investor execution or future intention. No second-quarter results or subsequent trial-status updates are included.

The current review should ask whether launch investments and manufacturing maturation create durable cash growth, whether margin pressure is temporary and how much value can be justified without the clinical asset. Events after this date are not evidence for answering those questions.

An exact transaction day remains unknown; the chronology documents public information availability rather than claiming that a market close identifies an investor's execution.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Evaluating an established medical franchise inside permanent capital
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/11144917/2026-Annual-Investor-Presentation.pdf; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260430478098/en/Pershing-Square-Announces-the-Closing-of-the-Combined-IPO-of-Pershing-Square-USA-and-Pershing-Square-Inc.; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/2055206659849437592
Date: 2026-05-15

The February11 presentation gives February9 gross core-fund AUM$19.748billion and core equity$16.077billion. PSH gross assets were$17.872billion and equity$14.202billion. These dated observations establish scale, not current June cash.

The April30 announcement of the combined PSUS/manager IPO reports$5billion aggregate gross proceeds. Fund and manager capital belong to different entities. It would be wrong to assume the whole offering is available to PSH, or to add it mechanically to old gross AUM as undeployed buying power.

Exact June deployment, vehicle-specific cash and current NAV weights were not independently recovered. Publicly discussed franchises include Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Brookfield, Uber, Universal Music, Restaurant Brands, Howard Hughes and Fannie/Freddie; Microsoft ownership was publicly discussed May15.

Those holdings illustrate a preference for durable economic roles, recurring cash and long-term reinvestment. They do not prove that any new healthcare candidate qualifies. Industry labels and the apparent stability of medical demand cannot substitute for evidence on pricing, competitive position, reinvestment and regulation.

The stated framework favors simple, predictable FCF, strong management, durable entry barriers, a sound balance sheet and limited capital-markets dependence. Alcon's installed workflows and consumables could fit that framework, while developmental clinical risk needs to remain separate.

The core company already generates substantial FCF and has multiple operating categories. A base investment forecast can therefore be built without assuming AURN001 approval. If the valuation requires that approval, the nature of the opportunity changes toward development-stage risk rather than an established compounder.

Concentration also requires assessing overlap in policy, consumer spending and currency factors. Vision care may diversify product-market demand relative to technology or restaurant franchises, but tariffs, manufacturing, healthcare access and innovation risk remain real.

No verified pre-June30 Alcon-specific Ackman thesis statement is supplied. The decision must be reasoned from current public operating evidence and prior principles. Permanent capital can tolerate a measured launch cycle, but should not be used to excuse an unbounded recovery timetable or an unpriced clinical dependency.
docs.D09_clinical_option_separate_from_base.m:
Title: AURN001 — a pivotal-stage option, not required core earnings
Source: compiled from: https://aurionbiotech.com/2026/04/08/aurion-biotech-doses-first-patients-in-astra-phase-3-study-evaluating-aurn001-in-patients-with-corneal-edema-secondary-to-corneal-endothelial-dysfunction; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1167379/000116737926000013/q42025pressrelease.htm; https://s1.q4cdn.com/963204942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/earnings-result/Q1-2026-Press-Release.pdf
Date: 2026-05-05

Aurion's April8 announcement states that the first patients have been dosed in ASTRA, a pivotal Phase3 study evaluating AURN001 for corneal edema secondary to corneal endothelial dysfunction. The relevant clinical proposition is restoring corneal clarity and vision through cell therapy, not a routine extension of an already approved US commercial product.

The announcement describes a randomized, double-masked study comparing treatment with placebo, enrolling at12 US sites. Its primary endpoint is the percentage of participants gaining at least15 letters, or three lines, of best-corrected visual acuity at month6. Secondary endpoints include changes in corneal thickness and visual acuity.

First-patient dosing is evidence of trial initiation, not efficacy, safety, completed recruitment, regulatory approval or commercial adoption. Later registry pages can display updated status and estimated completion dates; those later updates are not imported into this June freeze.

The base company already generated$1.733billion defined FCF in2025 and$279million inQ1. It sells surgical equipment, consumables, implantables, contact lenses and ocular-health products. A valuation can therefore start with an established operating business rather than an assumed future therapy launch.

That separation is essential. A base forecast should include ongoing R&D and the costs of supporting development, while assigning no unapproved sales unless clearly identified as an upside scenario. It should not count a potential therapy's revenue and simultaneously remove all associated clinical spending from normalized profit.

A separate option analysis would require probability of technical/regulatory success, addressable patient demand, treatment economics, capacity, reimbursement, ownership economics, launch timing and remaining investment. The source set does not support a defensible numerical expected value for those inputs.

Clinical failure would eliminate some potential upside and could leave sunk costs. It need not destroy the existing consumables/contact-lens franchise. Conversely, even a successful trial would not guarantee a rapid profitable launch.

The investment test is whether core recurring cash generation and a reasonable margin path justify the current price without the option. If not, describing the position as an uncomplicated predictable compounder would conceal its dependence on developmental risk. No later results or approval are assumed.

drivers.driver: Surgical installed-base economics produce sticky recurring consumable demand.
Demographics, income and access support durable vision-care growth.
Launch/R&D costs, tariffs, FX and lens-manufacturing maturation obscure higher structural margins.
De-rating toward18x earnings, buybacks and prospective EPS growth create attractive return potential.
AURN001 is incremental upside rather than required core value.

valuation.downside_case: Limited by share repurchases and consistent FCF generation; downside protected by dominant market position in eye-care.

drivers.driver: A high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative dominant player in the eye-care space with a recurring revenue model.
The valuation is attractive at 21.9x core EPS, representing a dislocation from its underlying quality and growth potential.
Management is actively driving shareholder value through a $1.5 billion share repurchase program and operational efficiency improvements.
A clear earnings growth algorithm driven by 5-7% sales growth in surgical and vision care segments.
The market is overly focused on transitory margin discrepancies and launch-related expenses rather than long-term intrinsic value.

kill_criteria: Clinical or regulatory failure of the AURN001 pipeline asset
Persistent margin compression failing to bridge the gap between reported and core operating results due to structural rather than transitory costs
Deceleration of surgical and vision care segment sales growth below the 5-7% target for two consecutive quarters
Material deterioration of the balance sheet or abandonment of the share repurchase commitment
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A failure of the AURN001 clinical program or a structural, non-transitory impairment to operating margins would invalidate our thesis.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant leader in the eye-care industry, providing essential surgical equipment, implantables, and vision care products [D01]. Its business model is exceptionally attractive, characterized by recurring revenue from consumables and high-moat surgical workflows that generate significant, predictable free cash flow [D01, D03].

We have identified a compelling entry opportunity due to a market dislocation centered on the gap between reported and core operating margins [D02, D05]. While the market is distracted by temporary launch-related expenses and regulatory uncertainty surrounding the AURN001 pipeline asset, it has overlooked the company's underlying earnings power and its demonstrated ability to raise guidance in the face of these headwinds [D03, D05, D07].

At our entry price, the stock trades at approximately 21.9x core 2025 EPS [D04]. Given the company's durable growth runway and dominant competitive position, we believe a 25x multiple is appropriate, supporting an expected IRR of 24% in our base case [D01, D03, D04].

Our role as investors is to benefit from the eventual re-rating of the company as the margin bridge closes and investors gain conviction in the 10-13% core EPS growth trajectory [D03, D05]. Management's disciplined capital allocation, specifically the $1.5 billion share repurchase authorization, provides a meaningful catalyst and floor to the valuation [D03].

We are mindful of the risks, particularly regarding the AURN001 pipeline, which represents a potential binary outcome [D05, D09]. However, the company's essential nature and strong cash flow profile limit our downside and provide a margin of safety [D01, D03].

We are initiating an 8% target position in the Company, as we are confident in its status as a high-quality compounder that is currently misunderstood by the market [D04].

valuation.eps_path: 10-13% annual constant-currency core EPS growth driven by margin expansion and share repurchases
valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 16-18x if margin expansion stalls or implantable growth remains sluggish

drivers.driver: A dominant, recurring-revenue healthcare franchise with a clear secular growth runway in the aging population segment [D01, D03].
We were able to acquire our stake at 21.9x core EPS, a discount to the intrinsic value of a high-quality compounder growing core EPS in the double digits [D03, D04].
Operating margins are expanding toward targets through disciplined cost management, rising to 21.2% in Q1 2026 [D02, D03].
Management's 10-13% core EPS growth algorithm is supported by operational leverage and a new $1.5 billion share repurchase program [D03].
The market is overly focused on short-term revenue volatility and implantable growth, failing to appreciate the resilience of the recurring surgical consumables model [D01, D03, D05].

kill_criteria: Management fails to achieve consistent margin expansion toward target levels over the next four quarters.
The surgical consumables attachment rate declines significantly, signaling a breakdown in the recurring revenue moat.
A catastrophic clinical or regulatory failure occurs regarding the AURN001 development program.
Capital allocation strategy pivots toward value-destructive M&A funded by excessive leverage.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the surgical consumables model is structurally impaired by competitive technology or that long-term margins cannot reach our projected terminal level due to permanent pricing pressure.
final.memo:
Alcon is the global leader in eye care, operating a dominant surgical and vision care business characterized by high barriers to entry and strong recurring revenue [D01]. The company's installed surgical workflows and clinical trust create a durable moat that benefits from long-term secular growth in aging populations and the rising prevalence of visual impairment [D01]. We view Alcon as a high-quality compounder that meets our standard for a simple, predictable, and free-cash-flow-generative business [D01, D02].

The market’s recent reaction to a revenue miss has created an attractive entry point for a franchise that remains fundamentally strong [D03, D05]. Investors are overly focused on temporary volatility in implantables growth and reported margin gaps, while failing to value the underlying resilience of the consumables business and the progress in core operating margin expansion, which reached 21.2% in Q1 2026 [D01, D02, D03, D05].

At our entry valuation of 21.9x FY2025 core EPS, we believe the stock is mispriced relative to its 10-13% core EPS growth trajectory [D03, D04]. With management’s focus on disciplined margin expansion and the benefit of a $1.5 billion share repurchase program, we expect significant earnings power accretion over the next three to five years [D03]. We anticipate a re-rating of the multiple toward 22x as the company delivers on its 2026 outlook [D03].

Our role is that of a long-term owner supporting management’s continued execution of their operational and capital allocation strategies [D03]. We expect the business to compound at a high rate as it leverages its installed base to drive steady demand for consumables while managing down its cost structure [D01, D03]. We maintain high conviction in the durability of this growth algorithm [D03].

The primary risks include a potential failure in the AURN001 program or a sustained deterioration in the surgical consumables capture rate [D05, D09]. We have established a target position of 8% of NAV to reflect our conviction in the company’s competitive dominance and its ability to navigate short-term extrinsic factors [D02].
